text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose modestly today, gaining nearly 0.9%, as oil refiners continued to benefit from elevated crude prices and robust refining capacity utilization. U.S. crude was trading at $97.26 per barrel—well above the pre-crisis baseline—and U.S. refineries are running at 97.8% capacity, near maximum levels. This combination of high oil prices and full utilization drives stronger margins for refiners like Marathon, even as the stock pulled back slightly from yesterday's $399.44 peak.

The broader backdrop is a volatile geopolitical situation: Saudi Arabia shut down a major pipeline after drone attacks this week, and while Trump signaled expectations of a near-term Iran war resolution that could lower oil prices, Iran's leadership rejected surrender, keeping the conflict unresolved and crude elevated. This uncertainty has kept energy markets buoyant over the past two weeks—Marathon is up 8.91% since early September—though intraday volatility remains high as investors weigh competing signals about when (or if) tensions will ease.
